scope: All three complete source reports personally reread; six targeted bone decisions. No global QA clearance.
exposure_disclosure: The coordinator received the audit agent's six-state retention summary before this source reread. This assessment is not blinded. It was frozen before opening the agent's detailed assessment/comparison artifacts. The coordinator did not author either original reader/reviewer annotation for these three cases. The audit agent authored the original batch001 review, so its reread does not add an independent pass there. Original source-based reader/reviewer provenance is preserved.

Contusion.evidence: Œdème osseux focal d'aspect partiellement linéaire sur la face latérale du condyle fémoral latéral portant, représentant une contusion osseuse ou une fracture microtrabéculaire non déplacée.

Fracture.evidence: Fracture non déplacée du coin postérieur du plateau tibial latéral avec extension intra-articulaire, sans marche d'escalier articulaire. Œdème léger de la moelle osseuse associé.

decisions.reason: The full French report separately diagnoses tibial-spine avulsion, intra-articular tibial plateau and fibular-head fractures with marrow edema, acute soft-tissue injuries and a large lipohemarthrosis. These support a current acute fracture weak positive independently of the ambiguous femoral contusion-versus-microtrabecular clause. That local alternative does not establish an unfractured impact contusion. It remains uncertain rather than importing the separate fracture decision.

decisions.reason: The complete Greek report describes degenerative medial-compartment disease and subarticular marrow edema with a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture. It supplies neither an impact mechanism nor acute fracture timing/discrete-line morphology. Both targets remain uncertain: the subtype is not an automatic fracture negative or a contusion positive.

decisions.reason: Explicit acute left-knee trauma and definite trabecular fractures at two sites in both findings and impression support an acute fracture weak positive under the frozen direct-diagnosis rule. This is report-level diagnostic evidence, not proof of a discrete line on images. All described traumatic marrow edema is associated with those diagnosed fractures, so a separate impact contusion without a fracture line is not established and remains uncertain. Do not automatically transfer the distinct microtrabecular-wording disposition of batch007 index48.
